attributes.residual: The rule stays. THE PER-WORD DECOMPOSITION, which the source comment approximates and this record makes exact. All 18 words are in 0xd4-0x218 and split into five webs: (a) 3 words - the first block's index*240 offset, target r25 against ours r24, at +0xd4 `mulli`, +0xdc `add r22,r31,rX` and +0x12c `add r4,r31,rX`; (b) 6 words - the second effect id, target r22 against ours r27, at +0x184 `lwz`, +0x190 `cmpwi`, +0x19c `cmpwi`, +0x1b0 `addi r4,rX,0`, +0x1c0 `mulli` and +0x218 `stw rX,3072(r3)`; (c) 4 words - the second EffectInfo entry pointer, target r23 against ours r22, at +0x1c4, +0x1c8, +0x1f0 and +0x20c; (d) 3 words - the second index*240 offset, target r26 against ours r24, at +0x1ec, +0x1f4 and +0x214; (e) 2 words - the second node cursor, target r24 against ours r23, at +0x1f8 and +0x204. The direction is uniform and is the mechanism: retail REUSES the registers of parameters that have just died - r27 held `typeIndex`, last read at +0x17c, and r26 held `pos`, last read at +0x1d8 - for the second block's temps, while ours allocates fresh registers from the low end (r22/r23/r24) and leaves the dead parameter registers alone. A source lever has to make the parameter webs die where retail's die, and the three axes the comment records are exactly the three that try to do it by restructuring the second block. Six rows in the aligned view are NOT differing words and should not be counted as residual: +0x54, +0x5c, +0x84, +0x1a4, +0x1ac and +0x1d4 differ only in relocation SYMBOL (`lbl_80114790`/`lbl_80348068` against our anonymous `@177`/`@13`), the instruction words are identical, and `wf_word_diff` reports RELOC-SYMBOL MISMATCH = 0.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Check whether retail's r27 and r26 really are the incoming parameters and really are dead at their reuse points. If either is still live past the reuse, the dead-parameter-reuse reading is wrong. Measured 2026-09-03 from the aligned view: target's r27 is written only by the prologue's `@0x20 addi r27,r4,0` (parameter 2) and last read at `@0x17c slwi r0,r27,2`, then rewritten at `@0x184`; target's r26 is written only by `@0x1c addi r26,r3,0` (parameter 1) and last read at `@0x1d8 addi r4,r26,0`, then rewritten at `@0x1ec`. Both reuses are immediately after the last read, so the reading holds.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes - every register named above, its defining instruction and its last-read offset were read from `fnasm --raw --diff` against the retail bytes over the whole 150-instruction body.
hypothesis.statement: The untried axis is the PARAMETER LIFETIME, not the block structure. All three exhausted axes restructure the second guts block; none of them changes when `typeIndex` and `pos` die. Copying both parameters into locals at the top of the function - or, conversely, moving the `colorIndex` block after the `typeIndex` block so the parameters die in the other order - changes the death points the allocator reuses, which is the only property distinguishing the two colourings.
